headline: A 2023 law lets foreign ship crew members stay in the U.S. for up to 180 days, instead of 29, when they perform certain ship-to-ship liquid cargo transfers.
what_it_does: The law allows an alien crewman, meaning a foreign crew member, to get a landing permit for up to 180 days. The permit applies only if the crewman will be doing ship-to-ship liquid cargo transfer work on a vessel engaged in foreign trade. Before this law, the longest such permit was 29 days.

who_it_affects.group: Foreign crew members on vessels engaged in foreign trade
who_it_affects.how: They can receive a landing permit lasting up to 180 days, rather than up to 29 days, if they will be doing ship-to-ship liquid cargo transfer work.
Their foreign crew members who handle ship-to-ship liquid cargo transfers may be allowed to stay in U.S. waters or ports for a longer permitted period.

who_it_affects.group: Immigration officials who issue crew landing permits
who_it_affects.how: They may issue permits covering longer periods for this specific type of crew work.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on January 5, 2023. The official summary does not state a separate effective date or any later deadline.
